lessons.title: Numbers and counting
lessons.description: Build the mathematical toolkit for statistics: use set notation and Venn diagrams, select counting methods, classify numbers and calculate accurately using PEMDAS.
coverage: Course introduction, evidence and sampling through the Mystery Bag demonstration.
Set membership, cardinality, empty and universal sets; union, intersection and complement; two-set Venn diagrams.
Basic counting principle, factorials, permutations and combinations; explain whether roles or order matter.
Natural, whole, integer, rational, irrational and real numbers.
Order of operations with powers, roots and nested brackets; diagnose equal-priority left-to-right errors.
objectives: Use basic set notation and calculate set operations.
Select and apply a suitable counting method.
Classify common real numbers after simplifying them.
Evaluate expressions using PEMDAS/BODMAS and explain the order of operations.

lessons.title: Calculations in context
lessons.description: Solve linear and simple quadratic equations, convert units, and use percentages and ratios to make and justify numerical decisions.
coverage: Variables, signed coefficients, constants and like terms; expressions versus equations; simplify, substitute and expand.
Solve linear equations by balancing both sides; verify by substitution.
Recognise quadratics and solve by factorisation or the quadratic formula.
Metric and imperial unit conversions, conversion factors and interpreting capacity limits.
Percentages of a whole, reverse percentages, discounts and percentage change using the starting value.
Simplify and scale ratios, split totals, distinguish part-to-part from part-to-whole, and recover a missing total.
objectives: Simplify algebraic expressions and solve linear equations.
Recognise and solve simple quadratic equations.
Convert measurement units with appropriate units and rounding.
Select the correct percentage or ratio method and interpret the result in context.

lessons.title: Applied problem solving
lessons.description: Apply the Week 1 toolkit to a connected product case, from customer evidence and product choices to packaging, material quantities and sales revenue.
coverage: GreenSip customer-feature survey: organise overlapping responses in a Venn diagram and distinguish the surveyed group from wider claims.
Count product combinations; choose permutations or combinations for testers and different roles.
Form and check a linear equation for bottle mass; convert batch mass and assess a planning limit.
Model rectangular packaging with a quadratic equation and choose physically valid dimensions.
Work backwards from production loss, divide materials in a ratio, calculate discounted prices and compare revenue with a target.
Complete an independent EcoCup transfer task and identify assumptions that still need evidence.
objectives: Choose and justify mathematical methods across a connected case.
Organise overlapping survey evidence and count product or team possibilities.
Solve contextual linear and quadratic equations and check units and dimensions.
Calculate quantities, losses, ratios, discounts and revenue.
Separate a correct calculation from a conclusion the evidence actually supports.

lessons.title: Populations, samples and variables
lessons.description: Identify the group being studied, distinguish sample statistics from population parameters, classify data and carry out simple random or systematic selection.
coverage: Population, sample and census; parameter versus statistic in relation to the stated research question.
Sample percentages as evidence about a wider population, with clear limits on what is known.
Categorical versus quantitative data; discrete counts versus continuous measurements; coded IDs and rounded measurements.
Simple random sampling from a complete list with distinct IDs; optional equal-individual-chance versus equal-sample-chance extension.
Systematic sampling: random start, interval N/n, sampling fraction n/N, selected IDs and reverse reasoning from later positions.
Repeating patterns in a sampling frame and differences between valid random samples.
objectives: Define a population and sample for a research question.
Distinguish a population parameter from a sample statistic.
Classify variables by what they measure, including numerical category codes and rounded continuous measurements.
Describe a valid simple random selection procedure.
Calculate systematic intervals, sampling fractions and selected positions, and recognise problematic list patterns.

lessons.title: Sampling methods and survey bias
lessons.description: Develop stratified and cluster sampling plans, distinguish chance variation from bias, and evaluate the reliability and practical cost of survey evidence.
coverage: Proportional stratified allocation, random selection within each group and fixed-total rounding; equal versus proportional group samples.
Cluster sampling of whole classes; comparison with stratified and simple random procedures.
Sampling variation versus bias; coverage/selection issues, nonresponse, leading questions and systematic measurement error.
Response rates versus support among respondents; optional logical bounds for unknown responses.
Accuracy versus precision using repeated-sample plots; why sample size does not repair biased procedures.
Select a defensible sampling method using cost, access and statistical limitations; evaluate and rewrite survey headlines.
objectives: Allocate a stratified sample and explain exactly how participants will be selected.
Distinguish stratified, cluster and simple random sampling from their procedures.
Diagnose selection, nonresponse, response and measurement problems and propose precise repairs.
Calculate response and respondent-support percentages using the correct denominators.
Distinguish accuracy from precision and defend a sampling choice with its main limitation.
Assess whether a survey claim is supported by the reported evidence.

lessons.title: Survey workshop
lessons.description: Investigate a canteen survey, check whether its claims follow from the data, repair its sampling and measurement methods, and write a defensible report.
coverage: Distinguish a reduction in portion size from a reduction in measured waste using a two-day pilot.
Calculate response rate, support among respondents and logical lower/upper support bounds among invitees.
Identify club-only coverage, leading wording and a miscalibrated scale; write a neutral survey question with balanced options.
Compare individual simple random selection with pair-based selection; reconstruct systematic sampling sequences.
Allocate proportional programme samples, interpret a realised cluster imbalance and diagnose programme-specific nonresponse.
Classify canteen variables, retain valid zeros, evaluate survey headlines and write a concise corrected report.
Seminar cases on changing population definitions, unequal sampling fractions, daytime-only contact, list periodicity and methods matched to study needs.
objectives: Audit numerical claims and distinguish descriptive comparisons from causal evidence.
Use correct denominators and missing-response bounds when interpreting survey support.
Repair biased or unclear selection, question wording and measurement procedures.
Justify a sampling design and examine what happens between invitations and replies.
Classify recorded variables and write a short report limited to what the evidence supports.

lessons.title: Tutorial: review, repair and prepare
lessons.description: Review numerical skills and sampling, revisit difficult steps and prepare for assessment.
coverage: The course website schedules review of numerical skills, sampling and frequency tables. No tutorial teaching files are present to verify the exact planned activities.

lessons.title: Centre, spread and distribution shape
lessons.description: Mean, median and mode; range, quartiles using n + 1, IQR and five-number summaries; interpret skewness and the effect of extreme values.
coverage: Mean, median and mode; sample and population mean notation
Effect of correcting, deleting or replacing an extreme observation
Range and why equal ranges can conceal different spread
Quartile positions using (n+1)p with linear interpolation; IQR and five-number summary
Positive, negative and symmetric distribution shapes; choosing suitable summaries
objectives: Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode, range, quartiles and IQR.
Distinguish a quartile position from its interpolated value.
Explain how extreme observations affect different summary measures.
Use the tail to identify skewness and justify a suitable measure of typical value and spread.

lessons.title: Understanding variation
lessons.description: Deviations, population and sample variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation and kurtosis; calculate and interpret absolute and relative spread.
coverage: Signed deviations and why deviations from the mean sum to zero
Squared deviations, population variance and standard deviation
Target population versus sample; sample variance using n−1 and sample standard deviation
Absolute versus relative variation; coefficient of variation
Kurtosis and the influence of extreme values; ordinary kurtosis benchmark of 3
Optional backwards problem finding missing values from the mean and sample SD
objectives: Calculate deviations, variance and standard deviation with appropriate units.
Select the population or sample variance method from the target group.
Interpret the mean, SD and CV together when comparing consistency.
Classify supplied kurtosis values and explain why equal SDs do not imply identical shapes.

lessons.title: Paper supplier workshop
lessons.description: Compare two suppliers using delivery-time averages, IQR, sample SD and CV; justify decisions for routine orders and changing deadlines. Formative Assessment 1 follows the workshop.
coverage: Revision of sample/population notation, centre, spread, quartiles, deviation, sample SD and CV
Two suppliers with 30 simulated delivery times each
Mean, median, range, (n+1)p quartiles, IQR, sample variance, SD and CV
Evidence-based recommendation for routine A4-paper orders
On-time counts and percentages at 48-hour and 54-hour deadlines
Trade-offs, remaining delivery risk and why minimum SD alone does not determine the best supplier
objectives: Analyse both suppliers using measures of typical delivery time and variation.
Write a recommendation supported by numerical comparisons and business meaning.
Reassess the decision when the delivery deadline changes.
Distinguish historical on-time percentages from a guarantee for the next delivery.

lessons.title: Organising and summarising data
lessons.description: Frequency and percentage tables, bar and pie charts, class intervals and midpoints, estimated grouped means, and stem-and-leaf plots.
coverage: Categorical frequencies, relative frequencies and percentages
Vertical and horizontal bar charts; pie-chart sector angles and construction
Nonoverlapping lower-inclusive upper-exclusive class intervals and class midpoints
Grouped frequency tables, modal class and midpoint-based estimated mean
Stem-and-leaf plots for integer and decimal data, including repeats and empty stems
Independent selection of class intervals and explanation of information lost through grouping
objectives: Construct frequency tables and suitable bar and pie charts.
Allocate values correctly to class intervals and calculate midpoints.
Estimate a grouped mean and explain why it may differ from the exact mean.
Create and interpret stem-and-leaf plots while preserving every original observation.

lessons.title: Distributions and relationships
lessons.description: Histograms, frequency polygons, cumulative tables and ogives; estimate medians, plot relationships, use a line of best fit and compare boxplots.
coverage: Equal-width histograms from raw data and the effect of changing interval width
Frequency polygons and relative-frequency comparisons
Cumulative frequency and cumulative percentage tables
Ogives at upper class boundaries; threshold counts and grouped median interpolation
Scatterplots, explanatory and response variables, association and causation
Straight lines of best fit, predictions and extrapolation limits
Five-number summaries and boxplots using (n+1)p quartiles
objectives: Build and interpret histograms, polygons and ogives using the correct horizontal values.
Estimate the median from cumulative percentages and explain the grouping limitation.
Plot paired data and interpret association without claiming causation.
Use and evaluate a straight-line prediction.
Construct and compare boxplots using medians and IQRs.

lessons.title: Campus café Excel practical
lessons.description: Use café data to build frequency tables, a bar chart, histogram and scatterplot in Excel; interpret the evidence and recommend how to reduce food waste.
coverage: Revision and classification of meal ID, meal type, satisfaction, item count, portion and leftover weights
Matched Demo (20 records) and Data (300 records) worksheet layouts
COUNTA, filtering distinct category labels, COUNTIF and fixed references
Category frequencies, shares and a bar chart
COUNTIFS for lower-inclusive upper-exclusive intervals, histogram and threshold counts
Scatterplot of portion and leftover weights; paired observations and association limits
Recommendation to reduce food waste, supported by figures, a chart and a satisfaction check
Optional cumulative-percentage graph outside the 90-minute core
objectives: Use Excel formulas to produce and check category and grouped frequency tables.
Create a labelled bar chart, equal-width histogram and scatterplot.
Explain when grouped data cannot give an exact count inside an interval.
Make an evidence-based café recommendation and propose a fair satisfaction check.

lessons.title: Sets, events and Venn diagrams
lessons.description: Sample spaces, set notation, complements, intersections and unions; probability from diagrams.
objectives: Describe a sample space and identify events within it.
Use union, intersection and complement notation to describe event relationships.
Calculate probabilities from labelled Venn diagrams.

lessons.title: Probability rules
lessons.description: Addition rules, mutually exclusive events and independence through worked and guided examples.
objectives: Use the addition rule to calculate the probability of a union.
Identify mutually exclusive events and explain the effect on the addition rule.
Distinguish independence from mutual exclusivity in contextual examples.

lessons.title: Applied probability practice
lessons.description: Use Venn diagrams and probability trees to solve multi-step problems and explain event relationships.
objectives: Represent a probability problem using a Venn diagram or tree.
Combine probabilities along and across appropriate branches.
Explain the event relationships used in a multi-step solution.

lessons.title: Tutorial: review, repair and prepare
lessons.description: Review descriptive statistics, charts and basic probability. Correct common errors through targeted questions and prepare for further probability work.

lessons.title: Conditional probability and trees
lessons.description: Conditional probability, multiplication rules, independence and sampling with or without replacement.
objectives: Calculate and interpret a conditional probability.
Use multiplication rules and tree diagrams for successive events.
Adjust probabilities for sampling with or without replacement and identify independence.

lessons.title: Discrete random variables
lessons.description: Construct a probability distribution and calculate expected value and variance; introduce binomial conditions.
objectives: Construct a valid probability distribution for a discrete random variable.
Calculate expected value and variance from a probability distribution.
Identify whether a situation satisfies the conditions for a binomial model.

lessons.title: Probability workshop
lessons.description: Use dice and practical examples, calculate binomial probabilities and interpret mean and spread.
objectives: Represent outcomes in dice-based and other practical probability problems.
Calculate binomial probabilities for specified numbers of successes.
Calculate and interpret the mean and spread of a binomial distribution.

lessons.title: Continuous variables and probability area
lessons.description: Measurement scales, continuous random variables, rectangular density models and cumulative probability F(x).
objectives: Identify measurement scales and distinguish continuous measurements from discrete counts.
Calculate probabilities as areas under a rectangular density model.
Interpret F(x) as cumulative probability and use it to find interval probabilities.

lessons.title: Normal distribution and z-scores
lessons.description: Normal curve properties, standardisation and probabilities using the standard normal distribution.
objectives: Describe the shape and key properties of a normal distribution.
Calculate and interpret a z-score.
Find lower-tail, upper-tail and interval probabilities using the standard normal distribution.

lessons.title: Applying the normal model
lessons.description: Solve probability and percentile problems using guided examples and independent practice.
objectives: Translate contextual questions into normal probability calculations.
Find a percentile or threshold by converting a z-score to the original measurement scale.
Interpret results with appropriate units and check whether an answer is reasonable.

lessons.title: Sampling distributions
lessons.description: Sampling variability, standard error and the Central Limit Theorem.
objectives: Distinguish the distribution of individual observations from a sampling distribution.
Calculate and interpret the standard error of a sample mean.
Explain how the Central Limit Theorem supports an approximate normal model for sample means.

lessons.title: Confidence intervals
lessons.description: Point estimation, confidence levels, margin of error and intervals using z and t.
objectives: Distinguish a point estimate from a confidence interval.
Select a suitable z- or t-based interval for a population mean.
Calculate a confidence interval and interpret its confidence level and margin of error.

lessons.title: Estimation workshop
lessons.description: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals, compare precision and explain conclusions in context.
objectives: Construct and interpret confidence intervals in context.
Compare interval precision and explain the effects of sample size and confidence level.
State a conclusion that acknowledges the uncertainty in the estimate.

lessons.title: Tutorial: review, repair and prepare
lessons.description: Review probability distributions, normal calculations and estimation. Revisit difficult methods and practise interpreting results in context.

lessons.title: Testing a claim
lessons.description: Null and alternative hypotheses, one- and two-tailed tests, significance levels and errors.
objectives: State null and alternative hypotheses using population parameters.
Choose a one-tailed or two-tailed test from the research question.
Explain significance levels and distinguish Type I from Type II errors.

lessons.title: One-sample tests
lessons.description: Apply z-tests and t-tests, calculate test statistics and interpret p-values.
objectives: Choose an appropriate one-sample z-test or t-test and state its assumptions.
Calculate a test statistic and obtain or interpret its p-value.
Use the significance level to decide whether to reject the null hypothesis.

lessons.title: Hypothesis testing workshop
lessons.description: Select a method, work through a complete test and communicate an evidence-based conclusion.
objectives: Organise a complete hypothesis test from a contextual question.
Apply a suitable test and justify the decision using sample evidence.
Write a conclusion in context and distinguish failure to reject from proof of the null hypothesis.

lessons.title: Comparing two groups
lessons.description: Independent and paired samples; frame hypotheses and choose an appropriate test.
objectives: Distinguish independent samples from paired observations.
Formulate hypotheses for a comparison of population means.
Choose a test that matches the study design and available information.

lessons.title: Two-sample and variance tests
lessons.description: Tests for population means with known or unknown variances; chi-square tests for population variance.
objectives: Select a method for comparing population means with known or unknown variances.
Calculate and interpret the test statistic for a two-sample comparison.
Use a chi-square test for a population variance and state its normality assumption.

lessons.title: Comparison workshop
lessons.description: Practise paired and independent comparisons, interpret results and check assumptions.
objectives: Carry out paired and independent-sample comparisons.
Check the assumptions needed for the chosen test.
Interpret the result and explain what it means for the original comparison.

lessons.title: Measuring relationships
lessons.description: Scatter plots, Pearson correlation and the distinction between association and causation.
objectives: Use a scatter plot to describe the direction, form and strength of a relationship.
Calculate or interpret Pearson correlation.
Explain why correlation alone does not establish causation.

lessons.title: Simple linear regression
lessons.description: Least-squares line, slope and intercept, predictions, model assumptions and R².
objectives: Interpret the slope and intercept of a least-squares regression line.
Use the fitted line to make a prediction and distinguish interpolation from extrapolation.
Interpret R² and identify the assumptions and limitations of the model.

lessons.title: Regression workshop
lessons.description: Analyse data in Excel, interpret regression output and evaluate the limits of a prediction.
objectives: Use Excel to analyse a relationship between two numerical variables.
Interpret the regression equation and relevant output in context.
Evaluate whether a prediction is justified by the observed data and model assumptions.

lessons.title: Tutorial: review, repair and prepare
lessons.description: Review hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Repair gaps in understanding and prepare for the mock assessment with targeted exam-style questions.

lessons.title: Descriptive statistics revision
lessons.description: Review sampling, summary measures, tables and graphs through mixed questions.
objectives: Select appropriate sampling methods, summary measures and graphical displays.
Calculate and interpret descriptive statistics in mixed questions.
Identify and correct errors in numerical summaries and graphs.

lessons.title: Probability and inference revision
lessons.description: Practise distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and regression; identify and correct common errors.
objectives: Choose suitable probability, distribution and inference methods for mixed problems.
Interpret estimation, hypothesis-testing and regression results in context.
Identify and correct common mistakes in method selection and calculation.

lessons.title: Mock assessment and feedback
lessons.description: Work through exam-style questions, explain methods and review solutions.
objectives: Complete exam-style questions and show a clear sequence of reasoning.
Use feedback to explain and correct mistakes.
Identify specific topics and methods that need further revision.

1.description: Build the mathematical toolkit used throughout statistics. Practise numbers, sets and counting, develop confidence with algebra, percentages and ratios, then apply these skills to a connected business case.
1.referenceDescription: Key terms and formulas for the week, with examples. Keep this reference sheet with your class handouts.

2.description: Start by identifying who and what we want to study. Compare ways to select a sample and recognise bias, then bring these ideas together to investigate a canteen survey and judge what its evidence can support.

3.description: Describe what is typical in a dataset and how much its values vary. Connect measures of centre, spread and distribution shape, then use them to compare two suppliers and justify a decision.

4.description: Turn raw data into clear tables and graphs. Develop the calculations behind each display, interpret distributions and relationships, then bring the methods together in a café data workshop using Excel.

5.description: Develop the language and rules of probability. Use sets and Venn diagrams to describe events, choose appropriate probability rules, and connect diagrams and trees in multi-step problems.

6.description: Explore how one event changes the probability of another. Build probability trees, describe discrete random variables, and apply probability distributions and the binomial model in practical situations.

7.description: Connect continuous measurements with probability areas. Move from rectangular density models and cumulative probability to normal distributions, z-scores and percentiles, then apply the models to contextual problems.

8.description: Use samples to learn about populations. Explore sampling distributions and standard error, construct confidence intervals, and explain how uncertainty and precision affect an estimate.

9.description: Evaluate claims using sample evidence. Form hypotheses, choose a one-sample test, and use significance levels and p-values to reach and communicate a conclusion.

10.description: Extend hypothesis testing to comparisons between groups and claims about variation. Distinguish paired from independent data, select suitable tests, and interpret results with their assumptions and limitations.

11.description: Explore relationships between numerical variables. Interpret scatter plots and correlation, build and use a regression line, then analyse results in Excel and evaluate the limits of predictions.

12.description: Bring the course together through targeted revision and exam-style practice. Review descriptive statistics, probability and inference, then use a mock assessment and feedback to identify the next steps in your preparation.
